sections.heading: When to use
sections.text: Use CLLC for bidirectional isolated DC-DC conversion. CLLC is symmetric — both primary and secondary have series L and parallel C. This enables ZVS on both sides for forward and reverse power flow.

sections.heading: Key difference from LLC
sections.text: CLLC has resonant tanks on both sides of the transformer. For reverse power flow, the secondary-side switches must be actively controlled (not just diodes). The gain curve is symmetric for forward and reverse operation.

sections.heading: Controller structure
sections.text: Frequency control same as LLC. For bidirectional operation, the controller must switch the active bridge roles when power flow reverses. The frequency command is the same for both directions; the phase relationship between bridges determines power direction.
